author: Dustin Nelson
title: State Fair has slowest day of 2026 on Tuesday - NewsBreak
text:
By Dustin Nelson ,
10 hours ago On Tuesday, Minnesota State Fair attendance again lagged behind admission numbers from recent years.
The fair brought 112,836 people through its gates on the only Tuesday of its 12-day run. That’s the lowest one-day total seen so far this year.
The record was set in 2019 with 145,022, about 12,000 more than last logged in 2025.
Minnesota State Fair in 2025Photo by Dustin Nelson/Bring Me The News
As noted yesterday , the late start date for this year’s Great Minnesota Get Together may play a role in lower weekday attendance, as many school districts in the state began their 2026-27 year this week.
In 2025, the fair’s final day was Sept. 1, and it was Sept. 2 in 2024. There are still six days to go this go-round.
Despite a couple of slow days to start the week, the 2026 fair continues to have higher attendance over its first six days than was seen over the last two years. Overall, 964,873 admissions have been tracked, slightly ahead of 2025’s 951,750 and more than 100,000 above the 2024 figure.
